name: id-stability-discovery
description:
Half of a pair: this scenario and id-stability-legacy serve the SAME endpoint -- 10.42.1.156, MAC 0050568b007f, hostname em-stable-01 -- through the two different Web API endpoints, and both assert the identical foreign id forescout-counteract:$HOST:170525084. If what the id means ever changes, exactly one of the pair fails and the other passes, which is the failure an existing deployment would experience as every asset re-keying.

The reason the two agree is that the CounterACT host key is the endpoint's IPv4 address packed into a 32-bit integer: the guide's own index example pairs hostId 170525084 with ip 10.42.1.156, and 10*2^24 + 42*2^16 + 1*2^8 + 156 is 170525084 exactly. The paginated endpoint's sample types the same key with an {EM.IP} placeholder in a block that also prints two "id" keys in one object, so the sample cannot be read literally -- which is why the id is canonicalised rather than trusted. Here it arrives in the address form and must still key on the integer; the second endpoint, arriving with the id already an integer, must pass through untouched. Note this is also why matchBehavior is no-id-match no-id-break: an address-derived key is recycled to whatever device takes the address over, so it is a record key and never a merge key.
